title: Regulations on Practice Where Individuals Hold More Board Directorships than They Can Handle
what_it_is: Regulations on Practice Where Individuals Hold More Board Directorships than They Can Handle

sections.label: Directors' duties and directorships
sections.summary: Directors must discharge duties responsibly, face enforcement for failure, and listed companies must disclose directorships and assess significant holdings.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: All directors, regardless of the number of directorships held, are required to discharge their duties responsibly, and with honesty and reasonable diligence.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: Those who fail to do so can face enforcement action, including disqualification and debarment.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: Singapore-listed companies are subject to additional requirements relating to board appointments, given the public interest involved.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: Under the Singapore Exchange's Listing Rules, they are required to disclose the directorships and principal commitments of individuals seeking to be appointed or re-elected to their boards.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: In addition, under the Code of Corporate Governance, where a director holds a significant number of directorships, the company's Nominating Committee and Board are to provide a reasoned assessment of the ability of the director to diligently discharge his or her duties.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: About 95% of directors of Singapore-listed companies hold no more than two directorships, and over 80% of directors hold only one directorship.

sections.label: UK Corporate Governance Code limits
sections.summary: The UK Code limits top executives to one FTSE 100 non-executive directorship, while chairs and non-executive directors must allocate sufficient time.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: The UK Corporate Governance Code limits top executives to only one FTSE 100 non-executive directorship.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: However, there is no such limit for chairs and non-executive directors, but individuals must allocate sufficient time to the company to discharge their responsibilities, which is similar to the requirements that we have under our Listing Rules.
